title: Mobile App Design & Development
metaTitle: Mobile App Design & Development · Artifact Digital
description: Mobile app design and development for iOS and Android — from an idea and a prototype through to a designed, accessible app people keep on their phone.
lede: iOS and Android apps, designed and built end to end. We start with what someone opens the app to do, then make that the easiest thing in it.
summary: iOS and Android apps, designed and built end to end.
intro: A phone is an unforgiving place to put an idea. People use apps standing up, one-handed, distracted, in bad light, often for less than a minute. Anything confusing gets deleted, and nobody writes to tell you why.

So we design for the one thing someone opens your app to do, and make everything else get out of its way. Fewer screens, bigger targets, clearer language, and a first run that doesn't demand a tutorial.
Sometimes the right answer isn't an app at all. A mobile website or a web app can do the job for a fraction of the cost, and we'll tell you when that's true before you spend the money.

sections.heading: Designed for real hands and real conditions
body: We build the experience around how people actually hold a phone: thumb-reachable actions, type that survives sunlight, targets you can hit while walking, and states for slow connections and no connection at all.

Accessibility is part of that, not a later pass. Proper contrast, text that scales when someone has increased their font size, labels that make sense to a screen reader, and motion that respects a reduced-motion setting.

sections.heading: Prove the idea before the full build
body: You can learn most of what matters from a version people can hold and tap, long before the app is finished. We build that early — real screens, real flows, on a real device — and put it in front of the people you're building for.
It's the cheapest moment to be wrong. Every change after the store release costs more, and a review takes days rather than minutes.

sections.heading: Getting it into the stores, and keeping it there
body: Shipping a mobile app includes the parts nobody enjoys: developer accounts, provisioning, store listings, screenshots, privacy disclosures, review feedback and the update cycle after launch.
We handle that with you, set up the accounts in your name, and keep the app working as the platforms change underneath it.

faq.q: Do I need a mobile app or a web app?
faq.a: If people need notifications, offline use, the camera or a home-screen icon they open daily, a mobile app earns its cost. If they'd use it occasionally on a laptop, a web app is usually faster and cheaper to build and change. We'll tell you which one your idea actually needs.

faq.q: Do you build for both iOS and Android?
faq.a: Yes, usually from one codebase so you're not paying twice for every feature. Where an app genuinely needs platform-specific work, we'll explain the trade-off before committing.

faq.q: Can you get it into the App Store for us?
faq.a: Yes. We set up the developer accounts in your name, prepare the listing and screenshots, submit, and handle review feedback. You keep the accounts and the keys.

faq.q: What if I just want to test the idea first?
faq.a: That's often the smartest first step. We can build a version real people can use on their phone without going through store release, learn from it, and only then decide what's worth building fully.

ctaHeading: Got an app idea worth testing?
ctaSub: Tell us what someone would open it to do. We'll help you work out whether it needs an app, and what the first version should be.
